sentences: Homer B. Hulbert was an American educator, writer, and missionary who truly believed in the future of Korea.
He first came to Korea in the late 1800s to teach at a royal school, but his work quickly went beyond the classroom.
Hulbert noticed that the Korean writing system, Hangeul, was logical and easy to learn.
While many Westerners didn't care about it, Hulbert praised Hangeul and studied it deeply.
He believed that promoting Hangeul and Korean culture could make the people stronger.
When Japan began taking control of Korea, Hulbert didn't keep quiet.
He wrote in international newspapers to say Korea should be free.
He also traveled to the U.S. and Europe to tell people about Korea and ask for independence.
His actions made him a trusted friend to many Koreans.
Even after he left Korea, Hulbert continued to help the Korean independence movement.
He returned to Korea in his later years and died in Seoul in 1949.
Today, he is remembered as a foreigner who loved Korea with deep respect.
Hulbert's story teaches us that true friendship and love can go beyond countries.

items.statement_ko: 헐버트는 한국의 미래를 진심으로 믿었던 미국인 교육자이자 작가, 선교사였다.
items.why_ko: 1번 문장에서 그를 미국인 교육자·작가·선교사로 소개하며 한국의 미래를 진심으로 믿었다고 했다.
_evidence_text: Homer B. Hulbert was an American educator, writer, and missionary who truly believed in the future of Korea.
items.statement_en: Hulbert was a teacher, writer, and missionary from America who really had faith in Korea's future.

items.statement_ko: 헐버트의 활동은 교실 안 수업에만 머물렀다.
items.why_ko: 그의 일은 곧 교실을 넘어섰다(went beyond the classroom)고 했다.
_evidence_text: He first came to Korea in the late 1800s to teach at a royal school, but his work quickly went beyond the classroom.
items.statement_en: Hulbert's activities stayed only inside the classroom where he taught.

items.statement_ko: 헐버트는 한글이 논리적이고 배우기 쉽다는 점을 알아차렸다.
items.why_ko: 3번 문장에 한글이 논리적이고 배우기 쉽다는 것을 알아차렸다고 나온다.
_evidence_text: Hulbert noticed that the Korean writing system, Hangeul, was logical and easy to learn.
items.statement_en: Hulbert saw that Hangeul made sense and was not hard to learn.

items.statement_ko: 당시 많은 서양인들도 한글에 큰 관심을 보였다.
items.why_ko: 많은 서양인들은 한글에 관심이 없었고(didn't care) 헐버트만 칭찬하며 깊이 연구했다.
_evidence_text: While many Westerners didn't care about it, Hulbert praised Hangeul and studied it deeply.
items.statement_en: At that time, many Westerners were also very interested in Hangeul.

items.statement_ko: 헐버트는 한글과 한국 문화를 널리 알리는 것이 사람들을 더 강하게 만들 수 있다고 믿었다.
_evidence_text: He believed that promoting Hangeul and Korean culture could make the people stronger.
items.statement_en: Hulbert thought that spreading Hangeul and Korean culture could make the people stronger.

items.statement_ko: 일본이 한국을 지배하기 시작했을 때 헐버트는 조용히 침묵을 지켰다.
items.why_ko: 헐버트는 침묵하지 않았다(didn't keep quiet)고 했다.
_evidence_text: When Japan began taking control of Korea, Hulbert didn't keep quiet.
items.statement_en: Hulbert stayed silent when Japan started to take control of Korea.

items.statement_ko: 그는 한국이 자유로워야 한다고 국제 신문에 글을 썼다.
items.why_ko: 7번 문장에 국제 신문에 그런 글을 썼다고 나온다.
_evidence_text: He wrote in international newspapers to say Korea should be free.
items.statement_en: He put his writing in newspapers around the world, saying that Korea should be free.

items.statement_ko: 그는 미국과 유럽을 다니며 한국을 알리고 독립을 호소했다.
_evidence_text: He also traveled to the U.S. and Europe to tell people about Korea and ask for independence.
items.statement_en: He went to the U.S. and Europe to tell people about Korea and ask for its independence.

items.statement_ko: 그의 이러한 행동 덕분에 그는 많은 한국인에게 믿을 수 있는 친구가 되었다.
items.why_ko: 9번 문장에 그의 행동이 그를 신뢰받는 친구로 만들었다고 했다.
_evidence_text: His actions made him a trusted friend to many Koreans.
items.statement_en: Because of what he did, many Koreans saw him as a friend they could trust.

items.statement_ko: 한국을 떠난 뒤에는 한국 독립운동을 돕는 일을 그만두었다.
items.why_ko: 떠난 뒤에도 독립운동을 계속 도왔다고 했다.
_evidence_text: Even after he left Korea, Hulbert continued to help the Korean independence movement.
items.statement_en: After he left Korea, he stopped helping the Korean independence movement.

items.statement_ko: 그는 만년에 미국으로 돌아가 1949년 미국에서 세상을 떠났다.
items.why_ko: 그는 만년에 한국으로 돌아와 1949년 서울에서 사망했다.
_evidence_text: He returned to Korea in his later years and died in Seoul in 1949.
items.statement_en: In his later years he went back to America, and he died there in 1949.

items.statement_ko: 오늘날 그는 한국을 깊은 존중으로 사랑한 외국인으로 기억된다.
_evidence_text: Today, he is remembered as a foreigner who loved Korea with deep respect.
items.statement_en: These days people remember him as a foreigner who loved Korea with deep respect.

items.statement_ko: 헐버트의 이야기는 우정보다 자기 나라에 대한 충성이 더 중요하다는 것을 가르쳐 준다.
items.why_ko: 진정한 우정과 사랑은 나라를 넘어설 수 있다는 것을 가르쳐 준다고 했다.
_evidence_text: Hulbert's story teaches us that true friendship and love can go beyond countries.
items.statement_en: Hulbert's story teaches us that being loyal to your own country matters more than friendship.
